title: Answers to Questions: 1- Rules Related to Covering the Feet 2- The Sultan of Brunei's Declaration of His Intention to Implement the Shari'ah
text:
(Series of answers of the scholar Ata Bin Khalil Abu Al-Rashtah, Ameer of Hizb ut Tahrir, to the questions of the visitors of his Facebook page)

Answers to Questions:

1- Rules related to covering the feet

2- The Sultan of Brunei's declaration of his intention to implement the Shari'ah

To Ahmad Owais

Question:

Assalamu Alaikum, our honourable Sheikh.

I hope you will answer my questions if you have some spare time, may Allah bless you:

The first question: from the book The Social System:

1- On p. 51, in the line before the last, the book says "And there is no necessity for her to cover the feet, since they are covered". Does this sentence mean that it is not obligatory to wear something that covers the 'awrah, "the feet", under the clothing of public life?

2- On p. 51 of the same book, line 8, it says "because the wide garment let down below until the feet is obligatory". Does the word "until" here not indicate that the feet are not included in the covering "the jilbab"... This is from a linguistic point of view; otherwise the previous paragraph confirmed the obligation of the covering, but for linguistic precision, would it not be better to say "until below the feet", which is more accurate?

The second question: Some reports appeared on Facebook that the Sultan of Brunei declared his intention to implement the Shari'ah and that he is making changes to the constitution for this purpose... So what is the reality of this matter? May you be blessed, our Ameer.

Answer:

Wa Alaikum Assalam wa Rahmatullah wa Barakatuh

First: the question of the feet:

1- The first sentence of your question: "And there is no necessity for her to cover the feet, since they are covered": yes, it means that there is no necessity for the woman to wear something that covers her feet under the clothing of public life if this clothing trails on the ground by a hand-span or a forearm's length, no more, as stated in the full paragraph from which the first sentence of your question was quoted.

2- The second sentence of your question: "because the wide garment let down below until the feet is obligatory" means that if the feet are covered with socks or the like, then it is sufficient for the clothing of public life to reach the feet without trailing on the ground below them, for the letting down (irkha') mentioned in the verse will then have been achieved. This is likewise clear in the full paragraph from which the second sentence of your question was quoted.

3- So that the picture becomes clear to you, I repeat to you the answer to the previous question:

(a- Women, especially in the desert, used to walk barefoot or wear a sandal or something similar that did not cover the feet completely, so the woman's feet would be uncovered unless she trailed her garment on the ground so that her feet would not be uncovered while walking. So when the Messenger of Allah (saw) forbade trailing the garment out of arrogance, Umm Salamah saw that if the woman's garment did not trail on the ground, then when she walked and moved her feet while walking, her feet would become uncovered, because the foot was not covered, as she walked barefoot or wore a sandal that did not cover it... So she asked the Messenger (saw) "Then what should women do with their hems?", because the women's jilbab or abaya used to trail on the ground so that their feet would not be uncovered... So the Messenger (saw) permitted them to let it down a hand-span, and then a forearm's length, beyond the feet, so that if she walked barefoot the feet would not be uncovered as long as the garment was let down below the feet, trailing on the ground... So the subject was: (trailing the garment for the sake of covering the feet...), that is, the question was for the sake of covering the feet. In other words, trailing the jilbab on the ground below the feet was for the sake of covering the feet. So the 'illah (reason) for trailing the garment on the ground in addition to letting it down is the covering of the feet, and the ma'lul (that which is caused) revolves with the 'illah in existence and non-existence. So if the feet are covered, the garment does not trail on the ground; rather it is sufficient for it to fulfil the meaning of the idna', that is, the letting down mentioned in the verse "to bring down over themselves [part] of their outer garments", that is, that the garment is let down until the covered feet.

b- As for from where Umm Salamah measured the hand-span or the forearm's length, the matter was "trailing the garment on the ground"; this is what Umm Salamah asked about, seeking clarification. She saw that if the garment did not trail on the ground, the feet would become uncovered while walking, and this is correct, for if the garment does not trail on the ground at all, and the woman walks barefoot or wears a sandal that does not cover the whole foot, then when the woman moves her feet in walking, parts of the feet will become uncovered... So the Messenger (saw) permitted her to let it down a hand-span on the ground, because the hadith is about trailing the garment, and the word "trailing" means on the ground, so it indicates that the hand-span that trails on the ground is, that is, from below the foot.

And I repeat that this is so that the foot is not uncovered while walking. So if the foot is covered with socks, it is sufficient to let the jilbab down to the top of the foot covered with socks, that is, it is sufficient down to the ankles as long as the rest of the foot is covered.) End quote.

Second: the subject of Brunei

Yes, something like what you said in the question was reported. However, the implementation of the rules of Islam is not the establishment of rigid hudud (prescribed punishments); rather it must be a correct implementation by a state that adopts Islam completely as a system for life, the state and society, so it implements Islam internally and carries it to the world by Da'wah and Jihad, and its security and safety are by the authority of the Muslims, and it is free of the influence of the Kafir colonialists.

And Brunei lacks that. Even the hudud which it was reported that it will implement, it said they are upon the Muslims and do not include the non-Muslims in its lands! And it is well known that Brunei is strongly open to the Kafir foreigners... Moreover, its security and safety are not by its own authority but by the authority of the West, especially Britain... Therefore the matter is no more than letting off the steam of the feelings of the Muslims there...

Your brother Ata Bin Khalil Abu Al-Rashtah
